title: ReasonEdit: Editing Vision--Language Models using Human Reasoning
claim: Letting users give reasoning during editing yields edits that generalize to intermediate rationales and shared error chains, which prior editors lack.
layout: 3 stacked panels plus comparison table, top-down, dashed boxes with before/after answers
description: The figure has a top-left checklist table comparing 'Ours' and 'Prior' VLM editors on four properties: human reasoning, image/text generality, rationale generality and chain-of-error generality. Ours gets green checks throughout. Prior gets red crosses on every row except image/text generality. A top-right peach panel shows the editing pipeline: a skin lesion photo with the question 'Benign or cancer?', a robot's wrong answer 'Benign', clinician feedback with the correct answer and green underlined reasoning, then a wrench-like editor icon. A middle blue panel, 'Rationale Generality', shows two dashed boxes. Each has a new image, a question, and an unedited robot with a red wrong answer next to an edited robot with a green correct answer. A bottom gray panel, 'Chain-of-error Generality', shows two VLM rows with latent chains of sub-questions. Red marks wrong answers and green marks corrected ones.
caption: Reasoning-enhanced VLM editing lets users provide detailed feedback and reasoning, enabling broader generalization.
abstract: Model editing aims to correct errors in large, pretrained models without altering unrelated behaviors. While some recent works have edited vision-language models (VLMs), no existing editors tackle reasoning-heavy tasks, which typically require humans and models to reason about images. We therefore propose ReasonEdit, the first VLM editor to let users explain their reasoning during editing, introducing a new, practical model editing setup. ReasonEdit continuously stores human reasoning in a codebook, and retrieves only relevant facts during inference using a novel topology-balanced multimodal embedding method inspired by network science. Across four VLMs on multiple rationale-based visual question answering datasets, ReasonEdit achieves state-of-the-art editing performance, ultimately showing that using human reasoning during editing greatly improves edit generalization.
